title: Don't give to get more
hookLine: do not give expecting to get more (74:6)

lines: AFTER EVERYTHING I DID FOR YOU.
cards: You know the gift with a string on it. The favor that comes back up in an argument six months later: after everything I did for you. The wedding present chosen to impress.
The donation made mostly for the plaque. The help offered so that, one day, help will be owed. Most giving has a little ledger behind it, even when we don't admit it.
Just after the call to arise, al-Muddaththir gives the Prophet a short instruction that goes straight at that ledger.

teach.h: MANN: A FAVOR, HELD OVER SOMEONE.
teach.b: Verse six is four words in Arabic: wa la tamnun tastakthir.

teach.h: DON'T GIVE TO GET MORE BACK.
teach.b: Don't give, seeking more. Tamnun comes from mann, which carries two ideas: to bestow a favor, and to remind someone of it, to hold it over them. Tastakthir means to seek more, or to count something as a lot.
Commentators read the verse in more than one way. One early reading, reported from Ibn 'Abbas, is the plainest: don't give a gift so that you'll get a bigger one back.

teach.h: DON'T COUNT YOUR DEEDS AS MUCH.
teach.b: Another: don't consider what you've done as much; don't stand before your Lord counting your good deeds as if they were a favor to Him. A third: don't remind people of the good you've done for them.

Many commentators say the verse holds all of these, the same habit seen from different sides: keeping score. The Qur'an returns to this in surah al-Baqarah: don't cancel your charity with reminders and hurt.
A gift held over someone isn't really a gift anymore; it's a loan with interest.

Then verse seven: for your Lord, be patient. The giving and the patience are a pair. If you give without expecting a return, you'll need patience, because sometimes nothing comes back: no thanks, no favor, no recognition.
The verse doesn't promise you'll be repaid by people. It removes the repayment from the transaction entirely. You give, you let it go, and you wait, if you wait at all, on Someone else.

how: Muslims are taught to give charity without reminding the recipient of it or expecting return, citing 74:6 and 2:264; many give secretly so that, as a hadith says, the left hand doesn't know what the right gave.

o: don't give seeking more, or hold a favor over anyone
don't give more than you can afford to lose
don't accept gifts from people you don't know

games.q: don't give to get more — tap the pairs.
p: a favor, or holding it over someone
don't give to get a bigger gift

s: commentators read 74:6 in only one way
readings include: don't give to get more, don't count your deeds, don't remind.
al-Baqarah says reminders and hurt cancel charity
a gift held over someone stops being a gift.
the verse promises that people will repay you
it removes repayment from the giving; verse seven asks for patience.

games.q: a friend you helped last year is arguing with you. you're tempted to say: after everything I did for you. what does 74:6 point to?
o: don't hold the favor over them.
games.why: one reading of wa la tamnun is exactly this: don't remind people of what you gave, and don't count it as much.

practice: Think of someone you could give to today, time, a meal, a ride, a kind word, and check gently for a string: do I want thanks, credit, a favor later? If you find one, don't scold yourself; almost everyone does.
Just notice it, picture cutting it, and picture giving without ever mentioning it.

wordCard.voice: Tamnun tastakthir. In 74:6, don't give seeking more: don't hold a favor over anyone, and don't count your good as much. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 74:6: don't give (or remind of a favor) seeking more.

carryVoice: Your line: give, don't count. A gift without a ledger is still a gift. See you tomorrow.
